statements.statement_en: On the Judicial Selection Committee, judges and lawyers should have more votes than ministers and Knesset members, even if the government has less say over who becomes a judge.
Israel should apply its sovereignty to parts of Judea and Samaria (the West Bank), even if this harms relations with Israel's allies.
Israel should stop trading with countries that are openly hostile to it, even if Israeli exporters and consumers lose out.
The Jewish character of the state should be anchored more firmly in law, for example in the oath of Knesset members and ministers, even if non-Jews feel less equal.
The state should not create or fund new heritage centers for individual communities — Tunisian, Yemenite, Iranian — even if their traditions are less well preserved.
It should be easier for the state to revoke the citizenship or residency of people convicted of terrorism, even if they are left stateless.
Yeshiva students should be drafted into the army or civilian service like everyone else, even if some of them leave their studies.

statements.title_en: Professional army instead of the draft
statements.statement_en: Compulsory military service should be replaced by a professional army of contracted soldiers, even if this requires greater spending on military salaries.
Tax and housing benefits should go first and foremost to those who did military or national service, even at the expense of those who did not serve.
Israel should restrict more strictly the entry and residence of foreigners, including citizens' spouses who come from the Palestinian territories, even if this separates some families.
The state should expand tax breaks for long-term savings — pensions and keren hishtalmut (tax-advantaged savings funds) — even if tax revenue falls.
Foreign workers should have fewer social rights than Israeli workers, even if this worsens their working and living conditions.

statements.title_en: Foreign states and international organizations in Israel
statements.statement_en: Israel should restrict more strictly the activity of foreign states and international organizations on its territory, even at the cost of conflict with the UN and allies.
Israel should reduce the number of foreign workers, even if construction, agriculture and elderly care become more expensive.
Reservists and veterans should receive more payments and benefits, even if this requires raising taxes.
Surrogacy and egg donation should be available to same-sex couples and single people, even if this contradicts Jewish religious law.
A woman should have the right to an abortion without approval from a hospital pregnancy-termination committee, even if there are more abortions.
Prison conditions for those jailed for terrorism should be made harsher — fewer visits, less television and fewer privileges — even if Israel faces international criticism.

statements.title_en: Funding schools without the core curriculum
statements.statement_en: Schools that do not teach the core curriculum (math, English) should not receive state funding, even if students' families have to pay more for tuition.
Getting a divorce should be easier, even if one of the spouses objects.
Non-profit organizations (amutot) should report to the state in more detail on their money and activities, even if this burdens small organizations.
Couples should be able to marry in Israel without a religious ceremony, even if the Chief Rabbinate does not recognize such marriages.
Wages and job protections of public sector employees should be cut to reduce government spending.
Politicians should gain more influence over how the courts work, for example over choosing the Supreme Court president, even if the courts become less independent.

statements.title_en: Separate spaces for men and women
statements.statement_en: Separating men and women should be allowed in state and municipal settings — swimming hours, events, study programs — even if this limits one sex's access at certain times.

statements.title_en: Who is registered as a Jew
statements.statement_en: The Population Registry should record as Jews only those recognized as Jewish under Orthodox Jewish religious law (halakha), even if some immigrants are not recognized as Jews.

statements.title_en: Public broadcasting: Kan and Galei Tzahal
statements.statement_en: The state should sell or close public TV and radio stations, such as Kan and Galei Tzahal (Army Radio), even if no broadcaster independent of advertisers remains.
Families searching for children who disappeared in the 1950s (the Yemenite children affair) should have the right to exhumation and genetic testing, even over the objections of other families.
A resident of an apartment building should have the right to install an electric-car charger or an elevator in the shared areas, even if most neighbors object.
Major sporting events should be broadcast on free channels, even if the holders of broadcast rights earn less.
Supreme Court hearings should be broadcast live, even if this affects how the parties and judges behave.
Rabbinical courts should be allowed to hear civil and property disputes when both sides agree, even if this weakens the role of secular courts.
Public transport should run on Shabbat, at least on a limited scale, even if this breaks the religious status quo.
The state should reduce its support for settlements in Judea and Samaria (the West Bank), even if this makes life there harder for settlers.
Much more housing construction should be allowed, even at the cost of building on open spaces and greater strain on infrastructure.
Citizens should be allowed to withdraw pension savings before retirement, even if they are left with less in old age.
Defamation laws should be relaxed, even if people find it harder to defend themselves against false accusations.
The state should recognize same-sex couples as families on an equal footing with others, even if this contradicts the religious views of some citizens.
Decisions about a teenager's medical treatment should stay with the parents, even if the teenager disagrees with them.
The state should lower barriers to imports and new competitors, even if local producers find it harder.
The requirement that an adoptive parent be of the same religion as the child should be abolished, even if the child is raised in a different faith.

statements.title_en: Adoption: single people and same-sex couples
statements.statement_en: Single people and same-sex couples should be allowed to adopt on an equal footing with married couples, even if this contradicts the religious views of some citizens.
Measures against terrorism and its financing should be tightened, even if people not involved in terrorism are caught by the restrictions.
The opposition should be guaranteed the chairmanship of key Knesset committees, even if this makes it harder for the coalition to carry out its policy.
The police and security forces should be given broader powers to arrest, search and use force, even if the risk of abuse grows.
Appointments to senior state posts should be vetted by an independent committee, even if this limits ministers' choice.
The police should be allowed to question suspects for longer without a lawyer, even if the risk of false confessions grows.
Access to loans and mortgages should be restricted more tightly, even if it becomes harder for people to buy a home.
New immigrants (olim) should receive more benefits and assistance, even at the expense of other parts of the budget.

statements.title_en: Protecting the weaker party to a contract
statements.statement_en: The state should intervene in contract terms to protect the weaker party — the consumer or the worker — even if this limits the parties' freedom to negotiate.
Public institutions should hire workers directly rather than through contractor companies, even if this costs the budget more.
People convicted of terrorism and their families should lose state social benefits, even if the family members themselves have done nothing wrong.
Publishing the names and personal details of victims, the dead and minors without consent should be prohibited, even if this limits media coverage of events.
Emergency measures introduced during a war should be lifted as soon as it ends, even if the threat has not fully disappeared.
The government should have the power to shut down foreign media outlets it considers a security threat, even without a court decision.
The state should cut funding to schools that refuse to admit children because of their ethnic origin, even if parents want their children taught only within their own community.

statements.title_en: Medical care for teenagers without parental consent
statements.statement_en: Teenagers from age 15 should have the right to receive medical care without their parents' consent, even if the parents are not told.
The state should have the power to confiscate property linked to criminal organizations or terrorism without a criminal conviction, even if innocent owners are harmed.
Ministers should be allowed to act against the opinion of the government's Attorney General, even if their decisions undergo less legal review.
A minister should choose their ministry's legal adviser personally, without a competitive process, even if the adviser becomes more dependent on the minister.
The Knesset should be able to re-enact a law struck down by the Supreme Court, even if citizens have fewer ways to challenge laws in court.
A person who has been indicted should not be allowed to head the government, even if a court has not yet found them guilty.

statements.title_en: Immigration rights for grandchildren of Jews
statements.statement_en: The right to immigrate under the Law of Return should be kept for grandchildren of Jews and their families, even if some immigrants are not Jewish under Orthodox religious law (halakha).
Child benefits and daycare subsidies should depend on whether the parents work, even if some children lose assistance.
Israel should be bound by international human-rights conventions and by the agreements it has signed, such as the Oslo Accords, even when they limit the government's freedom of action.

72.plus_en: Politicians have more influence on appointing judges; the Bar and sitting judges have less.
72.minus_en: Politicians have less influence; the Bar and sitting judges have more.

166.name_en: Territory under Israeli sovereignty and law
166.plus_en: Applies Israeli sovereignty or law to more territory.
166.minus_en: Applies Israeli sovereignty or law to less territory.

171.plus_en: Permits more economic and other ties with hostile entities and states, or designates fewer of them as hostile.
171.minus_en: Restricts economic and other ties with hostile entities and states, or designates more of them as hostile (e.g. declaring a state an enemy state).

165.name_en: Legal entrenchment of the state's Jewish character
165.plus_en: Entrenches the Jewish character of the state more strongly.

164.name_en: State support for Jewish identity and the Diaspora
164.plus_en: Gives more state support to Jewish identity programs and Diaspora ties.

184.name_en: Powers to revoke citizenship and status
184.plus_en: Makes it easier to revoke citizenship or residency status.

185a.plus_en: Increases the conscription of yeshiva and Haredi men (enlistment quotas, sanctions, 'service for all', limiting Torah-study deferrals).
185a.minus_en: Expands or entrenches exemptions or deferrals for Torah study or religious reasons.

185b.name_en: Length and breadth of general conscription and reserve duty
185b.plus_en: Lengthens compulsory or reserve service, raises the exemption age, or extends conscription to more groups of the general population (e.g. new immigrants).
185b.minus_en: Shortens compulsory or reserve service, abolishes conscription, or adds individual exemptions (conscience, gender).

187.name_en: Linkage of rights and benefits to service
187.plus_en: Ties rights and benefits more strongly to military or national service.

179.name_en: Admission of foreigners for entry and residence
179.plus_en: Makes it easier for foreigners to enter and stay.
179.minus_en: Makes it harder for foreigners to enter and stay.

276.plus_en: Increases state support for pension savings.

173.name_en: Activity of foreign states and international organizations inside Israel
173.plus_en: Allows foreign states or international organizations more physical presence or operations on Israeli territory.
173.minus_en: Restricts their presence or operations inside Israel.

180.plus_en: Allows more foreign workers or makes hiring them easier and cheaper.
180.minus_en: Allows fewer foreign workers or makes hiring them harder.

3.name_en: Benefits for soldiers, reservists and veterans
3.plus_en: Gives more benefits, payments and preferences to those who served and their families.
3.minus_en: Gives fewer benefits, payments and preferences to those who served and their families.

269.name_en: Reproductive autonomy and access to fertility technologies
269.plus_en: Widens reproductive choices and access to reproductive technologies.

92.plus_en: Gives prisoners more rights or milder conditions.
92.minus_en: Gives prisoners fewer rights or harsher conditions.

300.name_en: State control over NGOs and associations
300.plus_en: Adds oversight and disclosure requirements for NGOs and associations (including cults).

158.plus_en: Adds non-religious options for marriage and personal status.

215.name_en: Pay and status of public sector employees
215.plus_en: Raises pay and status of public employees.

71.plus_en: The judiciary and its leadership are more self-governing.
71.minus_en: The judiciary is subject to more external influence.

151.name_en: Role of religious norms in state and public life
151.plus_en: Religious law and norms govern more of the state and public sphere, including gender-segregated spaces.
151.minus_en: Religious norms govern less; more secular alternatives and fewer segregated spaces.

141.name_en: State ownership in the economy and media

314.name_en: Families' right to learn the fate of relatives
314.plus_en: Widens families' rights to find out what happened to relatives.

235.name_en: Rights of individual owners in shared property
235.plus_en: Gives individual co-owners more rights in commonly owned property.

142.plus_en: Makes more media content freely available to the public.
142.minus_en: Makes less media content freely available.

154.name_en: Powers of religious institutions and courts
154.plus_en: Gives religious institutions more powers and monopoly, extends Rabbinate and state control over religious bodies, or widens religious courts' jurisdiction.
154.minus_en: Reduces these powers, control or jurisdiction.

356.plus_en: Gives more benefits for public transport.

169.name_en: Support for and presence of settlements in Judea and Samaria
169.plus_en: Increases support for and presence of settlements.
169.minus_en: Reduces support for and presence of settlements.

275.plus_en: Gives more possibilities to withdraw pension savings.

136.plus_en: Strengthens protection against defamation and sanctions for speech.

204.name_en: LGBT rights and recognition of non-traditional families
204.plus_en: Gives LGBT people more rights and protection, or recognizes non-traditional families more.
204.minus_en: Gives fewer rights or less recognition.

265.plus_en: Minors can decide more for themselves.
265.minus_en: Minors can decide less for themselves.

25.plus_en: Increases competition, lowers entry barriers, limits concentration and market power, or makes public procurement more open.
25.minus_en: Reduces competition, eases limits on concentration, or adds exemptions from competitive procurement.

309.name_en: Right to family life and adoption
309.plus_en: Removes obstacles to family life and widens possibilities to form a family by adoption.
309.minus_en: Adds obstacles and narrows such possibilities.

178.plus_en: Adds measures and sanctions against terrorism and its financing.

75.plus_en: Guarantees the opposition more seats and powers.
75.minus_en: Guarantees the opposition fewer seats and powers.

77.name_en: Powers and resources of security and law enforcement
77.plus_en: Broadens powers to detain, search, surveil and use force, adds resources or discretion for security forces.
77.minus_en: Narrows such powers, resources or discretion.

340.plus_en: Gives appointment vetting committees a larger role.

90.name_en: Procedural rights of suspects and defendants
90.plus_en: Gives suspects and defendants more safeguards.

31.plus_en: Gives more benefits and incentives for aliyah and to olim.
31.minus_en: Gives fewer benefits and incentives for aliyah and to olim.

352.plus_en: Gives more weight to the text of the contract.
352.minus_en: Gives courts more room to intervene in contracts.

283.plus_en: Private actors and intermediaries perform more public functions and social services.

277a.name_en: Denial of benefits and rights as a sanction
277a.plus_en: Denies or revokes benefits, allowances, licenses or other state rights from people as a sanction: those involved in terror and their families, illegal residents or infiltrators, boycott supporters, convicted officials.
277a.minus_en: Restores such benefits or rights, or limits the state's power to deny them as a sanction.

146.plus_en: Protects privacy and personal data better.
146.minus_en: Protects privacy and personal data less.

130.plus_en: Extends emergency measures or makes more legislation depend on a declared state of emergency.
130.minus_en: Shortens emergency measures or reduces legislation's dependence on a state of emergency.

137.name_en: State powers to restrict media and online content
137.plus_en: Gives the state more powers to restrict media and internet content.
137.minus_en: Gives the state fewer such powers.

161a.plus_en: Lets religious (esp. Haredi) schools and higher-education tracks set curriculum, admissions and gender separation without state conditions on funding.
161a.minus_en: Conditions funding on core curriculum, non-discriminatory admissions, or not inciting against military service.

101b.plus_en: Gives parents more control over their child's medical care, education, documents and monitoring, or eases custody/guardianship rules for parents.
101b.minus_en: Gives minors more autonomy (e.g. medical consent from 15) or lets the state remove or restrict parental guardianship (e.g. violent parents).

231e.name_en: Confiscation of property of criminals and terrorists
231e.plus_en: Expands the state's power to confiscate or forfeit property, money or assets of criminals, criminal organizations or terrorists, or of their supporters.
231e.minus_en: Narrows or limits such confiscation or forfeiture powers, or adds protections for owners and third parties.

63.name_en: Powers and weight of the Attorney General
63.plus_en: The Attorney General gets more powers or their opinions become more binding.
63.minus_en: The Attorney General gets fewer powers or their opinions become less binding.

60.name_en: Political control over state bodies and appointments
60.plus_en: Ministers and the cabinet control more; appointing bodies are freer; oversight bodies, regulators, legal advisers and prosecutors depend more on politicians.
60.minus_en: State bodies, legal advisers and prosecutors become more independent; appointments are bound by criteria.

66.plus_en: Courts decide more, have more discretion, review the executive and the Knesset more, and Knesset laws are less protected from judicial invalidation.
66.minus_en: Courts decide less, are bound by minimums and rigid frameworks, review less, and Knesset laws are more protected.

58.plus_en: The Prime Minister has more freedom of action.
58.minus_en: The Prime Minister has less freedom of action.

183.plus_en: Makes citizenship and aliyah easier to obtain.

277c.name_en: Eligibility for pregnancy, child and parent benefits
277c.plus_en: More people qualify for pregnancy, maternity, child, single-parent, alimony, daycare or foster-care benefits, or conditions are relaxed.
277c.minus_en: Fewer people qualify or conditions become stricter (e.g. child allowances limited, daycare subsidy conditioned).

296a.name_en: Commitment to international human-rights law and peace agreements
296a.plus_en: Adopts or reinforces international human-rights, refugee or humanitarian-law treaties, international courts, or signed diplomatic agreements and UN bodies.
296a.minus_en: Withdraws from or overrides such treaties, agreements or UN bodies (e.g. cancelling the Oslo Accords, revoking UNRWA immunities, rejecting WHO regulations).
